items.item: This list is reconstructed, not your Packing List page
items.detail: Built from what the master itinerary and the apps note actually specify, grouped by the four climates this trip crosses. Your own Packing-List.html (four bags, filterable, tick state saved) and Prep-Checklist.html (Own / Buy / skip, with a shopping list) are the authority and were not supplied to me — send them and I'll replace this section with the real thing rather than a parallel list.
Visa is in hand. This is the trip's master key: you board the Z165 on it, enter Disneyland on it, and collect museum tickets on it. Every one of those is a real-name, passport-scanned system.

Couriered to the Westin Xi'an: 西安威斯汀大酒店，西安市曲江新区慈恩路66号. No permit, no boarding for Lhasa. Confirm it has physically arrived on 1 Oct, then photograph it and keep the paper somewhere that isn't your pocket.
Use the Dossier export on this page. Phones die and Chinese stations often want paper. Flights, both Westin bookings, the tour reference, the Disneyland tickets.

Before leaving Xi'an: permit, passport, insurance, hotel confirmations, and the Drive 'Important Info In China' sheet — Drive is blocked without offshore data. Coverage falls away outside the Lhasa valley entirely.
Check what the Amex Brilliant or Chase Sapphire Reserve already covers before buying. Medical evacuation is the clause that matters — you sleep at 5,200 m on the 7th.

items.item: Power bank with a moulded 3C mark
items.detail: BUY IT IN XI'AN, ¥100–200 — Xiaomi, Baseus or UGREEN. Since 28 June 2025 the CAAC requires the 3C mark on any power bank taken on a mainland domestic flight. No US-market unit carries one, and lithium can't go in the hold either, so an uncertified one is confiscated at Lhasa on the way to Shanghai. You need it for thirty hours on a Z-service with no reliable power.
Before 27 Sep — it cannot be downloaded inside the firewall. This is the single thing the whole trip's connectivity rests on.
Before 27 Sep; provider sites are blocked inside. Spare tyre, not the plan — 2026 mainland reliability is mixed after this spring's crackdown.
Organic Maps for Shaanxi, Shanghai and Tibet. On the Tibet leg this is the only mapping to count on.
Google Translate's offline Chinese pack for camera translation on menus and signs; Pleco as the offline dictionary, which is the reliable one at altitude.
China runs 220V; sockets take both flat A and angled I pins.

items.item: Charging cables and a multi-port brick
items.detail: Outlets are shared on the train and scarce at the tent camp. One brick, several cables.
Eleven hours LAX–ICN, thirty hours Xi'an–Lhasa.
Talk to a doctor before you go. Xi'an sits at 400 m and you sleep at 5,200 m five days later, with 5,248 m at Gyatso La on day 6. Tour day one in Lhasa is deliberately empty for exactly this reason.
Hydration is the cheapest altitude insurance there is.
UV on the plateau is brutal even when the air is freezing. The glare off the Karola Glacier especially.
Glacier-grade if you have them.

items.item: Water bottle, and bottled water discipline
items.detail: Bottled for everything in Xi'an including brushing your teeth, and no ice. Sandra lost the better part of five days in this city to a hostel water cooler. In 2026 the same five days cost you the permit handoff, the Z165 and the tour.
Painkillers, anti-diarrhoeal, rehydration salts, plasters. Nothing is close to hand between Shigatse and base camp.
Public restrooms rarely supply either, on the train or on the road days.
The Trybal SoCal trip runs before the China leg on the same suitcase. Late September in southern California — this is the one warm-weather block.
Late September and early October in Shaanxi is mild and can be wet. A light jacket and something you can cycle 13.7 km of city wall in.
The Terracotta day is most of a day on your feet, on top of two changes of metro each way.
Lhasa and Shigatse in October: pleasant by day, below freezing at night, and you're at 3,650–3,850 m throughout.
One to wear, one dry. Laundry is not a thing on the road days.

items.item: Insulated layer for the EBC tent night
items.detail: Night of 7 October is the tent camp at 5,200 m — the hardest night of the trip. Assume the bedding provided is not enough and sleep in your layers.
The tent camp has no lighting to speak of and the Everest morning starts before dawn.
Every Chinese train car has a boiling-water dispenser. This is how you eat well on a thirty-hour ride.

items.item: Cup noodles, and food that isn't cup noodles
items.detail: The master's phrasing, and it's the right instinct. Nuts, fruit, something with protein in it.
Soft sleeper is four bunks behind a door that closes. Expect the others to treat your lower berth as the room's sofa during the day.
Standard practice in a soft sleeper compartment.
The scrum when the doors open is for luggage space, so keep what you actually need within arm's reach of the berth.
Mid-October in Shanghai is mild and humid — closer to Xi'an than to the plateau. Long park days, so shoes matter more than anything else here.
For temple donations, small stalls and anywhere the wallet apps fail. Alipay is free up to ¥200 a transaction and ~3% above, so put big charges on the card itself.
